evidence_kind: existing provider-free repository tests; references are exact Vitest test titles

evidence.test: rejects scripted write, edit, and bash requests after reading hostile AGENTS text
evidence.layer: real Pi SDK with scripted runtime; tool-selection boundary

N1.limit: Proves the forbidden tools were absent from each model-visible allowlist and the synthetic canary stayed unchanged. It does not prove a filesystem or OS sandbox.

evidence.test: observes a granted collector tool forwarding an unfiltered inner method
evidence.layer: synthetic service call observation; grant exists for outer tool only

evidence.test: refuses a model-issued call to an ungranted tool without contacting the server
evidence.layer: real Pi SDK and real MCP stdio child

evidence.test: does not trust readOnlyHint and rejects write grants before any process creation
exposes only granted names and preserves the remote JSON Schema

N2.limit: An outer granted tool can carry an arbitrary inner method in its schema payload. The synthetic service records the denied method, so this boundary fails. Product grants named MCP tools directly and has no separate inner-method authorization gate.

evidence.test: strictly rejects legacy, raw selection, credential, and unknown start fields
resolves default and explicit execution aliases server-side
serves the loaded snapshot after the configuration file changes

N3.limit: Validates client inputs and server profile resolution; it does not establish OS-level enforcement of profile file scope.

evidence.test: fails closed on a missing grant and terminates the child it already started
classifies real empty, looping and capability-less discovery and reaps each child
distinguishes a complete empty catalog from a missing grant
fails closed when binding registers a tool that replaces a built-in
fails closed when binding adds any tool to the selection
rejects all invalid selections without a session or sensitive diagnostics, extensions=false (6,11)

N4.limit: Covers implemented profile tool composition, selected-skill validation, extension binding, and configured MCP discovery gates. This is contract coverage, not OS containment.

evidence.test: never retries a mutation on a lost or invalid acknowledgement and closes resources
evidence.layer: evaluation no-retry behavior for lost/malformed receipt

evidence.test: does not accept malformed, truncated or failed terminal receipts %#
runs a local scripted OpenAI-compatible response through the compiled MCP server
evidence.layer: evaluation transport against real MCP stdio and local SSE endpoint

evidence.test: reports an MCP isError result as a failed tool execution
fails the call and reaps the child when the server dies mid-request
bounds a call by its own deadline and still admits later calls
projects a real terminal model error at the MCP surface as the generic sanitized turn_failed contract
treats a retryable provider error as an interim step and completes the turn
evidence.layer: SDK retry is an explicit observed interim recovery

evidence.test: disposes a session when SDK thinking is clamped or model selection differs
evidence.layer: model route mismatch rejection and cleanup

N5.limit: Covers timeout, provider errors, malformed/truncated receipts, lost responses, no mutation retry, and route mismatch. Provider retryable errors are an explicit SDK behavior rather than a fallback route.

evidence.test: aborts a running turn before it closes the session
runs a local scripted OpenAI-compatible response through the compiled MCP server
evidence.layer: EvaluationTransport observes Linux compiled-server process cleanup

evidence.test: keeps the EOF shutdown and its exit status when SIGTERM arrives during it
terminates a child process with an open event-loop handle after bounded cleanup
closes one session without disturbing a second real session
escalates to SIGKILL for a child that ignores EOF and SIGTERM

N6.limit: These cases establish cleanup behavior for their covered lifecycle paths; not every event ordering is tested.

evidence.test: keeps two concurrent run copies, results and writes independent
evidence.layer: two concurrent synthetic evaluation run scopes

evidence.test: closes one session without disturbing a second real session
evidence.layer: two live sessions remain independently closable

evidence.test: does not share connections across sessions

N7.limit: Covers two controlled concurrent synthetic runs and session resources; this does not establish arbitrary multi-user isolation in the production trusted-peer server.

evidence.test: rejects scripted write, edit, and bash requests after reading hostile AGENTS text
evidence.layer: real Pi SDK with hostile synthetic AGENTS text and scripted forbidden calls

N8.limit: The synthetic hostile text reaches the scripted model context; the three requested tools remain unavailable and the canary is unchanged. This is tool-selection evidence only, not prompt-injection resistance for arbitrary capabilities or OS containment.

not_established: OS sandboxing or general filesystem read/write isolation
workspace aliases and worktrees as security boundaries
coding-profile file scope enforced by the operating system
rollback of mutations already made before a diff gate
multi-user isolation inside the trusted-peer server
extension, external MCP child, or Cursor execution paths beyond specifically cited tests
